I will keep it simple and do what fits Quzhou best: I will plant the same land in a `winter wheat -> summer maize` rotation. In Quzhou, that is the familiar grain pattern, and it matches the local climate, machinery timing, and what people already know how to manage. I am assuming I have `20 mu` of grain land, so I will use the same `20 mu` twice in the year: wheat in the winter season and maize in the summer season.

I will not spread myself across too many crops. With my education level and the need to avoid mistakes, I would rather do two crops I understand and manage them steadily. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, not an old traditional seed, because local work in Quzhou is centered on winter wheat and summer maize and shows this system can produce well. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of chasing extreme yield, use `3` irrigations on wheat because wheat in this area needs more water support, and I will do `2` pesticide applications mainly for weeds, aphids, rust, and later disease prevention. For summer maize, I will use a hybrid because maize hybrids are standard for yield and uniformity. I will sow it immediately after wheat harvest with no-tillage to save time and keep moisture, use `2` irrigations, and keep `2` pesticide applications for weeds and major insects or leaf disease. I am setting yield targets below the Quzhou demonstration fields, because those fields use tighter technical management than I would count on for my own ordinary farm. Sources I used: Ministry of Agriculture fertilizer guidance for North China wheat and Huang-Huai-Hai maize, and Quzhou field reports showing the county’s wheat-maize system and recent local yield levels: https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm , https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230915_6436565.htm , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/col/col46309/index.html , https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html
